The next Vancouver civic election is on October 17, 2026.
Update: All in one page by Fairview / South Granville Action Committee: “ Getting to Know the Parties: Closing Summary, Updates & Election Information .”
Over the coming weeks, CityHallWatch will republish weekly excerpts of analysis of the main civic parties and mayoral candidates, as announced in “ CityHallWatch launches civic party intro series, courtesy of FSGAC .” The content is courtesy of the Fairview/South Granville Action Committee . The second in this series is the new Bright Future Vancouver party. For more election coverage and resources, please visit our election portal page here .
FSGAC e-mailed the following analysis to their subscribers on August 20.
With Vancouver’s municipal election approaching on October 17 , the Fairview/South Granville Action Committee is continuing our weekly series introducing the municipal parties and their mayoral candidates.
Our goal is straightforward: use publicly available news sources to provide residents with factual information about the choices before them so that they can do their own research, compare the alternatives and make an informed decision.
Last time, we looked at ABC Vancouver and Mayor Ken Sim, including ABC’s four-year record in office. This newsletter, we turn to Bright Future Vancouver (BFV) , a new municipal political party offering itself as an alternative to the established parties at City Hall.
Introduction
Bright Future Vancouver ( official website ) is a new civic political organization , registered by Elections BC in January 2026. Its candidates have never held elected office in Vancouver, so there is no Council record to evaluate.
BFV describes itself as a movement for “the people who make Vancouver work,” including workers, renters, families, seniors, young people, newcomers, community organizations and small businesses. The party says it was created in response to rising housing costs, affordability concerns, public safety issues and a growing perception that City Hall is disconnected from residents.
The party traces its origins to Muhammad Ahmad’s experience during the BCGEU strike, which it says reinforced his belief in communication, consensus-building and responsive leadership. BFV presents itself as a new voice in Vancouver politics , explicitly rejecting what it describes as the “same old script” at City Hall.
The party’s campaign slogan is particularly direct: “Vancouver is no longer for sale. It’s for us.” Its platform, called The Blueprint, describes itself as a plan “for the working class, funded by the few, built for the many.”
Because BFV is new, voters cannot evaluate it against a previous term in office. Instead, the key questions are whether its proposed policies are practical, affordable and achievable, and whether its candidates have the experience necessary to implement them.
Mayoral Candidate
Muhammad Ahmad

Kano gov appoints special advisers, others, fixes inauguration for Monday
News
January 5, 2025 7:14 pm
File: Kano State Governor, Abba Yusuf
By Tukur Muntari, Ted Odogwu
Kano State Governor, Alhaji Abba Yusuf, has announced a fresh round of appointments and reassignments, aimed at enhancing governance across the state.
In a statement released by his spokesperson, Sanusi Tofa, on Sunday, Yusuf announced that Ahmad Muhammad has been appointed Special Adviser on Publicity.
“Hon. Ahmad’s experience in grassroots governance and party organisation makes him a valuable asset to our administration’s communication efforts,” the statement read.
Yusuf also appointed Ahmad Ishaq as Special Adviser on Works, reinforcing the administration’s focus on infrastructure.
“Engr. Ishaq’s track record in project execution will be pivotal to our development drive,” the governor remarked. Make PUNCH part of your everyday experience. Add us to your Preferred Sources
Meanwhile, Tijjani Goje was elevated to Special Adviser, Lagos Liaison Office.
Yusuf emphasised the importance of this role, stating, “With Tijjani Kaura Goje’s extensive experience, I am confident he will effectively represent Kano’s interests in Lagos, fostering stronger inter-state cooperation.”
The appointments also include Sani Tofa as Special Adviser on Special Duties. 109 children die as measles spreads to 14 states

Diphtheria: 29 Katsina LGs affected, Kano confirms two deaths
“Malam Sani’s distinguished service in the judiciary and civil service positions him uniquely to oversee critical assignments for the state,” the statement highlighted.
Additionally, Ibrahim Fagge was named Chairman of the Local Government Service Commission, while Ladidi Garko was appointed Chairperson of the Kano State Civil Service Commission.
Both were formerly Commissioners of Finance and Tourism.
The governor’s spokesperson confirmed that the swearing-in will take place on Monday, January 6, 2025, at 11am in the Ante-Chamber of the Kano Government House.
The event will also see the inauguration of seven commissioner nominees recently screened by the Kano State House of Assembly, along with the newly appointed advisers.
“These appointments reflect Governor Yusuf’s dedication to assembling a team capable of delivering results and addressing the needs of the people of Kano State,” the statement concluded.Our

Interview with Muhammad Ahmad
Muhammad Ahmad (formerly Max Stanford Jr.) was a pivotal figure within the Black Liberation Movement and struggle for Black Power in the 1960s and 70s; notably, he was the national field chairman of the Revolutionary Action Movement (RAM) and a direct target of J. Edgar Hoover’s COINTELPRO. In this interview with Naji Mujahid of the DC Radio Co-op, he discusses how he became involved and reflects on his involvement as well as the current state of affairs in the Black community. Currently, he is a professor at Temple University
